```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(fisherscore)
```

## Side by side

`compare_glm()` fits a model with `stats::glm()` and with both `fs_glm()`
engines, then reports how far apart they are.

```{r}
compare_glm(cbind(ncases, ncontrols) ~ agegp + alcgp, binomial, esoph)
```

`summary()` output is laid out like `summary.glm()`:

```{r}
fit <- fs_glm(breaks ~ wool + tension, family = poisson, data = warpbreaks, engine = "cpp")
summary(fit)
summary(glm(breaks ~ wool + tension, family = poisson, data = warpbreaks))$coefficients
```

## Accuracy across families, links and data sets

```{r}
ucb <- as.data.frame(UCBAdmissions)
men <- MASS::menarche
set.seed(651)
sim <- data.frame(x = rnorm(500))
sim$y <- rbinom(500, 1, 1 - exp(-exp(-0.5 + sim$x)))   # complementary log-log truth
sim$count <- rpois(500, (2 + 0.5 * sim$x)^2)

models <- list(
  "esoph, logit"            = list(cbind(ncases, ncontrols) ~ agegp + alcgp + tobgp, binomial(), esoph),
  "menarche, probit"        = list(cbind(Menarche, Total - Menarche) ~ Age, binomial("probit"), men),
  "simulated, cloglog"      = list(y ~ x, binomial("cloglog"), sim),
  "warpbreaks, log"         = list(breaks ~ wool * tension, poisson(), warpbreaks),
  "UCBAdmissions loglinear" = list(Freq ~ (Admit + Gender + Dept)^2, poisson(), ucb),
  "simulated, sqrt"         = list(count ~ x, poisson("sqrt"), sim, start = c(2, 0.5)),
  "mtcars, gaussian"        = list(mpg ~ wt + hp + factor(cyl), gaussian(), mtcars)
)

tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  m <- models[[nm]]
  cmp <- do.call(compare_glm, c(m, times = 1))
  s <- cmp$summary
  data.frame(model = nm,
             iter_glm = s$iterations[1], iter_fs = s$iterations[3],
             max_coef_diff_R = s$max_coef_diff[2], max_coef_diff_cpp = s$max_coef_diff[3],
             max_se_diff_cpp = s$max_se_diff[3],
             dev_diff_cpp = abs(s$deviance[3] - s$deviance[1]))
}))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 20, format.args = list(digits = 2))
```

The sqrt-link model is given starting values. Without them, `glm()` and
`fs_glm()` both stop with *"no valid set of coefficients has been found"*,
because the first Fisher scoring step makes some $\eta_i < 0$, which is
invalid for $\mu = \eta^2$, and there is no earlier iterate to halve back
towards:

```{r}
try(glm(count ~ x, poisson("sqrt"), sim))
try(fs_glm(count ~ x, poisson("sqrt"), sim))
```

The pure-R engine reproduces `glm()` exactly: both build the same working
weights, run the same LINPACK QR, and follow the same stopping rule. The C++
engine uses LAPACK's Householder QR, so it differs by only a few units of
machine precision ($\approx 10^{-15}$). Both engines take the same number of
iterations as `glm()`.

## Speed

The script `inst/benchmarks/benchmark.R` times all three methods for
$n$ from $10^3$ to $10^6$ and $p \in \{5, 50\}$. Results saved by the script:

```{r}
res_file <- system.file("benchmarks", "results.csv", package = "fisherscore")
if (nzchar(res_file)) {
  res <- read.csv(res_file)
  wide <- reshape(res[, c("family", "n", "p", "method", "median_sec")],
                  idvar = c("family", "n", "p"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(wide) <- sub("median_sec.", "", names(wide), fixed = TRUE)
  wide$speedup_cpp_vs_glm <- wide$glm / wide$fs_cpp
  knitr::kable(wide, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
png_file <- system.file("benchmarks", "benchmark.png", package = "fisherscore")
if (nzchar(png_file)) knitr::include_graphics(png_file)
```

Most of `fs_glm()`'s time outside the engine goes on building the model
matrix, which `glm()` also does. The `time` element of a fit isolates the
Fisher scoring loop itself:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
n <- 2e5
d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n))
d$y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + d$x1 - 0.5 * d$x2))
c(R = fs_glm(y ~ ., binomial, d, engine = "R")$time,
  cpp = fs_glm(y ~ ., binomial, d, engine = "cpp")$time)
```
